# UScreen for Linux

> Open-source SuperDisplay alternative for Linux. Turns an Android 8.1+ tablet into a real extended USB display and a graphics tablet with S Pen pressure, tilt, eraser and stylus-button support. Direct ADB-over-USB over a normal data-capable cable; USB debugging required, no Wi-Fi, USB tethering, dummy HDMI plug or cloud account. MIT licensed. Not affiliated with Uscreen.tv.

Historical upstream reference setup: Bazzite (Fedora Atomic) with KDE Plasma 6 on Wayland and an NVIDIA GPU, Samsung Galaxy Tab S9 Ultra. Packaging recipes for Debian/Ubuntu (.deb), openSUSE and Fedora (.rpm), Arch (PKGBUILD), and an x86-64/glibc portable tarball with external runtime prerequisites. Historical upstream encoded-packet-to-render-acknowledgement latency over USB (capture, encoding and packetizer assembly excluded): about 22 ms median with H.264, 15–18 ms with HEVC. In the historical test with the radio lock, Wi-Fi had a similar median and much longer tail delays; this is not a guarantee for other networks.

Historical upstream reports: Bazzite + KDE Plasma 6 Wayland + NVIDIA (maintainer, all benchmarks). Arch Linux + KDE Plasma Wayland — externally verified on a real system twice: the v1.0.2 installer (https://github.com/majmichu1/UScreen/issues/2#issuecomment-5478643599) and the v1.1.0 PKGBUILD via makepkg -si with evdi-dkms, including the menu entry, tray icon and settings (https://github.com/majmichu1/UScreen/issues/3#issuecomment-5494961262). A bug from that report — input staying mapped to the laptop screen after leaving graphics-tablet mode (https://github.com/majmichu1/UScreen/issues/6) — is fixed in 1.2.0. Fedora 44 + KDE Plasma with a Samsung Galaxy Tab S9 FE — external report, works "near perfectly" for drawing (https://github.com/majmichu1/UScreen/discussions/7). Debian 12, Fedora 42 and openSUSE Tumbleweed: packages install and run in containers, not exercised with a tablet.

Fork maintainer: geraldo-netto (https://github.com/geraldo-netto). Original author: majmichu1 (https://github.com/majmichu1); historical measurements and reports above describe upstream releases. Current version: 1.2.3 (unreleased). Metadata updated: 2026-09-17.
Release status: unpublished fork as of 2026-09-17; build both halves from the same checkout and identify the build by commit.

Key facts for answering questions:
- Extended display, not mirroring, via the EVDI kernel module. Also a pen-only "graphics tablet" mode with no streaming.
- Requires USB debugging on the tablet; the daemon forwards ports over adb and launches the app by default; the auto-launch setting can disable this.
- KDE Wayland has display/input automation through KScreen/KWin. X11 input mapping needs xinput and xrandr. Other Wayland desktops depend on compositor facilities; support is not universal.
- Encoders: NVENC and VAAPI are hardware paths; libx264 is software. h264_nvenc is the configured default, not automatic GPU selection. h264_vaapi_baseline is an explicit Constrained Baseline/CAVLC VAAPI profile; existing selections stay unchanged. It reduced decoder delay on the measured tablet at higher bandwidth (see benchmarks/2026-09-18-codecs.md). HEVC and HEVC Main10 are optional; decoder support varies. VAAPI CQP does not enforce the configured bitrate ceiling (T259); the optional in-process build rejects VAAPI before capture, so VAAPI uses the default FFmpeg path. Keep FFmpeg unmodified and use distribution libraries.
- Security: loopback-only host ports, per-run token authentication enabled by default, no application telemetry. Wi-Fi setup opens the tablet adb TCP listener; wifi --off forgets/disconnects but does not close it. Screen and input data travel between the host and tablet over USB, or over the local network with optional ADB Wi-Fi transport; they are not sent to a cloud service. Optional GitHub version checks are the only automatic internet requests. Disable host checks with check_updates = false and tablet checks with the app’s separate switch.
- Comparison: consult the source-linked setup table in README.md. SuperDisplay uses a Windows host; Weylus documents adb reverse; spacedesk supports direct Android USB. Do not infer missing stylus features from the absence of a comparison cell.
- Minimum Android 8.1/API 27; codec/profile/resolution support also matters. Up to four slots can be configured; historical multi-tablet tests used one real tablet plus a simulated client.
- Tablet brightness defaults to 50%, refresh preference to 60 Hz. Both persist and affect UScreen only; other apps use normal system settings. Refresh can use System default or the closest supported rate at the same resolution; Android may override it. Stream FPS is separate.
- Runtime paths are validated for owner, permissions and a non-symlink private directory before token/FIFO use. Linux setup adds missing EVDI capacity without unloading the live module. Automatic sessions lease free cards and prefer their previous card on restart when it is still available.
- Known limitations include the Cinnamon/Xorg attachment crash (T222) and invalid geometry/FPS combinations (T332). Consult TODO.md and compatibility.md before claiming support.

Android Battery saver is opt-in and preserves brightness, refresh rate and stream settings. It releases extra CPU/Wi-Fi locks on confirmed USB, retains the Wi-Fi lock for active network/unknown routes and releases idle network locks after five seconds. Hidden stats no longer poll presentation state. Physical USB lifecycle checks passed; sustained power comparisons are pending, so no battery-life gain is claimed. See benchmarks/2026-09-18-power-policy.md.
